x: God the Most High means by His statement:
h
O you who have believed

: O you who have acknowledged the Oneness of God and the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Do not precede God and His Messenger means: Do not rush to decide a matter in your wars or your religion before God and His Messenger decide it for you, lest you decide contrary to the command of God and the command of His Messenger. It is narrated from the Arabs that someone precedes his leader, meaning he hastens to command or prohibit before him.
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, although their wording differed in explaining its meaning.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Do not put yourself before God and His Messenger
, meaning: Do not say anything contrary to the Book and the Sunnah.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
O you who have believed
, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger… the verse. He said: They were forbidden to speak before His speech.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed

, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, he said: Do not make an attempt to attack the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with anything until God decrees it through his tongue.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
O you who have believed

, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger. It was mentioned to us that some people used to say: If such and such had been revealed, such and such would have been removed. So God, the Almighty and Majestic, disliked that and put it forward. Al-Hasan said: Some Muslims slaughtered before the
h
O you who have believed
, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger,
h
and fear God

. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of Sacrifice, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to slaughter again.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed

, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, he said: Some people used to say, If only it had been revealed about such and such, if only it had been revealed about such and such. Al-Hasan said: They were people who slaughtered before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to slaughter again.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
O you who have believed

, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, meaning by that in fighting, and among their affairs was that which could not be decided except by His command, which was among the laws of their religion.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
O you who have believed
, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, he said: Do not decide the matter before God and His Messenger. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan,
h
O you who have believed

, do not precede God and His Messenger. He said: Do not decide a matter without the Messenger of God. The reciters of the regions read it with a damma on the ta’ in the phrase do not precede. This is the reading which I do not permit any contradiction to, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. It has been reported from the Arabs that they said: I preceded in such-and-such and I advanced in such-and-such. Based on this language, if it had been said: Do not precede with a fatha on the ta’, it would have been permissible. And His statement, “
h
And fear God
. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.” He says:
h
And fear God

, O you who believe, in your speech, lest you say what God or His Messenger has not given you permission to say, and in other matters of yours, and be mindful of Him, for God is Hearing of what you say, Knowing of what you intend by your speech when you say it. Nothing of what is in your hearts is hidden from Him, and other matters of yours and the matters of others.

evidence.text: The reciters of the regions read it with a damma on the ta’ in the phrase do not precede.
This is the reading which I do not permit any contradiction to, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Messenger of God, speaking harshly to him or speaking harshly to him.
h
And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another

. He says: And do not call him as you call one another: O Muhammad, O Prophet of God, O Prophet of God, O Messenger of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another
, he said: Do not call out to him loudly, but speak softly, O Messenger of God.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another
, they used to speak loudly and raise their voices, so God admonished them and forbade them from doing that.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Qatada
m: that they used to raise their voices and speak loudly in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they were admonished and forbidden from doing so.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet… the verse

, it is like His statement, Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of one of you to another (al-Nur 24:63). God forbade them from calling him as they call one another and commanded them to honor him and respect him, and to call him, if they called him, by the name of prophethood. Abu Kurayb narrated: Zaid Abu Thabit bin Thabit Qais bin Ash-Shammas narrated: My paternal uncle Ismail bin Muhammad bin Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas narrated on the authority of his father, who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak loudly to him,’ Thabit sat in the road weeping. Then Asim bin Adi of Banu Al-Ajlan passed by him and said: ‘What makes you weep, Thabit?’ He said: ‘Because of this verse. I fear that it was revealed about me, as I have a loud voice.’ So Asim bin Adi went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and weeping overcame him. Then he went to his wife Jamila bint Abdullah bin Abi bin Salul and said to her: ‘When you enter my horse’s house, tie a nail to the reins.’ So she struck him with a nail until he came out and he turned away and said: ‘I will not come out until God takes me or the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is pleased with me.’ Asim came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him what had happened. He said: ‘Go and call him for me.’ Then Asim went to the place, but did not find him. So he went to his family and found him in the horse’s house. He said to him: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is calling you. He said: Break the lizard. So they went out and came to the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What makes you cry, Thabit? He said: I have a loud voice, and I fear that this verse was revealed about: “Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak loudly to him.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Are you not satisfied to live a praiseworthy life, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise? He said: I am satisfied with the glad tidings of God and His Messenger. I will never raise my voice against the Messenger of God. Then God revealed: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God - those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety... the verse. Ibn Humayd narrated: Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shimr ibn Atiyyah, who said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Ash-Shammas came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was sad. He said: O Thabit, what do I see with you? He said: I recited a verse last night, and I fear that it has rendered my deeds worthless: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above

x: God Almighty says: Those who refrain from raising their voices before the Messenger of God. The root of ghad is to refrain from speaking softly. And from it: lowering the gaze, which is refraining from looking, as Jarir said: Turn a blind eye, you are from Namir. You have not reached Kaab nor Kalb. And His statement,
h
Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety

, God Almighty says: These are the ones who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God, and they are the ones whose hearts God has tested by testing them, so He chose them and purified them for piety, meaning for fearing Him by performing His acts of obedience and avoiding His disobedience, just as gold is tested by fire, so its good is purified and its bad is removed. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
God tested their hearts
, he said: Be sincere.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
God tested their hearts
, he said: God purified their hearts in what He loved. His saying,
h
For them is forgiveness
, means that they will have from God pardon for their past sins, and a pardon from Him for them. And a great reward, means that they will have a generous reward, which is Paradise.

x: God Almighty says to his prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, those who call to you from behind your chambers… Chamber is the plural of chamber, and three is a stone, then it is pluralized and said: chambers and rooms.

i: Some Arabs pluralize stone as rooms with a fatha on the jim, and likewise every plural of three to ten on fa’al they pluralize it as fa’al with a fatha on the second, and the nominative is more eloquent and better, and from this the poet said:
x: Wasn't Ibad worthy of the drama of Balli and the verses of Al-Hujurat?
He says: Yes, and for the Banu Hashim. His saying,
h
And most of them do not reason

, means: Most of them are ignorant of the religion of God, and what is necessary for them is your right and your respect. He mentioned that this verse and the one after it were revealed about a group of Bedouins who came calling to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind his rooms: O Muhammad, come out to us.
The narrator mentioned that:

c: Abu Ammar al-Marzouqi and al-Hasan ibn al-Harith told us: Al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Baraa’,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and said: O Muhammad, my praise is adornment, and my blame is disgrace. He said: That is God, blessed and exalted.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa,
m: with a similar narration, except that he said: That is God Almighty.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arfa narrated to us: Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman Al-Taymi narrated to us:
m: I heard Dawud Al-Tafawi say: I heard Abu Muslim Al-Bajali narrating on the authority of Zayd bin Arqam who said: “Some Arabs came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them said to each other: Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we will be the luckiest people because of him, and if he is a king, we will live in his wing. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that. Then they came to the room of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and began to call out to him: O Muhammad! So God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason.’ He said: Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of my ear and stretched it out, and began to say: God has fulfilled your word, O Zayd. God has fulfilled your word, O Zayd.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Abi Yahya Al-Muqaddami told us: Affan told us: Wahib told us: Musa bin Uqbah told us on the authority of Abu Salamah: Al-Aqra’ bin Habis Al-Tamimi told us that
m: he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and called out to him, saying: O Muhammad, my praising you is adornment, but my cursing you is disgraceful. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: Woe to you, that is God. Then God revealed: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers… Muhammad bin Amr told me:

c: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason. those who call to you from behind the chambers: the Bedouins of Banu Tamim.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and called out to him from behind a stone, saying: ‘O Muhammad, my praise is an adornment, and my cursing is a disgrace.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: ‘Woe to you, that is God.’ Then God revealed: ‘Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason.’”
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: “His statement, ‘Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers…’… the verse. It was mentioned to us that a man began to call out, ‘O Prophet of God, O Muhammad.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said, ‘What is the matter with you?’ He said, ‘By God, his praise is adornment, and his censure is disgrace.’ So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘That is God.’ So the man turned away, and it was mentioned to us that the man was a poet.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Umrah, who said:
m: Bishr bin Ghalib and Labid bin Uttar, or Bishr bin Uttar and Labid bin Ghalib, were sitting with Al-Hajjaj. Bishr bin Ghalib said to Labid bin Uttar: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers was revealed about your people, Banu Tamim. I mentioned that to Saeed bin Jubair, and he said: If he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered him: They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. They said: We have become Muslims, and Banu Asad did not fight you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind his rooms and said: ‘O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: ‘What is the matter with you? What is the matter with you?’ He said: ‘You know that my praising you is adornment and that my blaming you is ugliness.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘That is God’s will.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet.’” The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement, from behind the rooms. The regions recited it with a damma on the ha’ and the jim from al-hujurat, except for Abu Ja’far al-Qari’, who recited it with a damma on the ha’ and a fatha on the jim, as I described, the plural of al-hujr is hujr, then the plural of al-hujr is hujrat. The correct reading for us is to pronounce both letters with a damma, as described before.

x: And His statement,
h
And if they had been patient until you came out to them

, it would have been better for them, God Almighty says: And if these people who call to you, O Muhammad, from behind the chambers, had been patient and did not call to you until you came out to them when you came out, it would have been better for them in the sight of God, because God has commanded them to respect and honor you, so by not calling to you they are leaving what God has forbidden them from. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, God Almighty says: God is Forgiving of the one who calls to you from behind the veil, if he repents from disobeying God by calling to you likewise, and returns to God’s command in that and other matters, and He is Merciful to him that He does not punish him for his sin after he has repented from it.

God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, If a wicked person comes to you with information about a people, then verify it. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement fatabayyinu. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it fatabattu with a tha’, and it was mentioned that in Abdullah’s copy of the Qur’an it is dotted with a tha’.

Some of the reciters read it fatabayyinu with a ba’, meaning: wait until you know its authenticity, do not rush to accept it. This is also the meaning of fatabattu. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Uqba bin Abi Mu’ayt.
Mention the reason why this was said:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, on the authority of Thabit,
m: the freed slave of Umm Salamah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a man to collect the alms of Banu al-Mustaliq after the battle. The people heard about that and met him, venerating the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Satan told him that
m: they wanted to kill him. He returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Banu al-Mustaliq have withheld their alms. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims became angry. The people heard of his return. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and lined up before him when he had prayed the noon prayer. They said: ‘We seek refuge in God from the wrath of God and the wrath of His Messenger. You have sent us a man to collect alms.’ We were pleased with that and our eyes were comforted by it. Then he returned from some of the way, and we feared that this was wrath from God and His Messenger. They continued speaking to him until Bilal came and called the call to the afternoon prayer. He said: ‘And this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed if you are a believer, then indeed God wills.’” A wicked person has come to you with report, so verify it, lest you harm people out of

x: God Almighty says to the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Know, O believers in God and His Messenger, that among you is the Messenger of God. So fear God lest you say falsehood and fabricate lies, for God informs him of your report and makes him aware of your information, and his people are on the right path in their affairs. And His statement, If he had obeyed you in much of the matter, you would have been cursed, God Almighty says: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had acted in accordance with your opinions and accepted from you what you said to him, he would have obeyed you. You means: he would have suffered hardship and difficulty in many matters because of his obedience to you. If he had obeyed you, because he used to make mistakes in his actions, as if he had accepted what Al-Walid ibn Uqbah said about Banu Al-Mustaliq: They had apostatized, refused to pay the zakat, and gathered forces to attack the Muslims.

So he attacked them and killed some of them, and seized their blood and wealth. He had killed, and you had killed, those whom it was not permissible for him or for you to kill, and he had taken and seized from the wealth of a Muslim people what it was not permissible for him or for you to take, so he had suffered from God because of that.
h
But God has endeared faith to you

in God and His Messenger. So you obey the Messenger of God and follow him, and God thereby protects you from the hardship that if you had not obeyed him and followed him, and he had obeyed you, he would have suffered and befallen you. And His statement,
h
And He has made it pleasing in your hearts
, meaning: And made faith good, so you believed.
h
And He has made hateful to you disbelief

in God, and immorality, meaning lying, disobedience, meaning doing what God has forbidden in opposition to the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and neglecting what God has commanded.

Those are the ones who are rightly guided, meaning: These are the ones to whom God has made faith beloved, and has made it pleasing in their hearts, and has made hateful to disbelief, immorality, and disobedience. Those are the ones who are rightly guided and follow the path of truth. And His statement, Blessing and favor from God, means:
h
But God has endeared faith to you

, and bestowed upon you this blessing which He considered a favor from Him, and a kindness and favor from Him that He bestowed upon you. And God is Knowing and Wise, means: God has knowledge of who among you does good and who does evil, who is worthy of God’s favor and favor, and who is not worthy of it, and there is wisdom in His management of His creation, and His dispensing of them as He wills of His judgment. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, “
h
And know that among you is the Messenger of God
If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in trouble,” the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And know that among you is the Messenger of God

… the verse until he reached you have been cursed. These are the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If the Prophet of God had obeyed them in many matters, you would have been cursed. By God, you are the most foolish in opinion and the most reckless in mind. The most suspicious man is his opinion, and he who takes the advice of the Book of God is trustworthy for whoever takes it and adheres to it. Anything other than the Book of God is deception.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us:
m: Muammar recited Qatadah’s verse, If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be cursed. He said: You are the most foolish in opinion and the most foolish in dreams. A man may be accused of his opinion, but he seeks advice from the Book of God. And also as we said in the interpretation of his saying,
h
But God has endeared faith to you
, they said.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
He has made faith beloved to you and has beautified it in your hearts
, he said: He has made it beloved to you and made it beautiful in their hearts. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, “
h
And He has made hateful to you disbelief
, immorality, and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided. * A bounty and favor from God.” They also said.

x: Who said that?
h
And know that among you is the Messenger of God

. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in trouble. But God has endeared to you the faith and made it pleasing in your hearts and has made hateful to you disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And He has made disbelief and immorality hateful to you

, he said: Lying and disobedience. He said: Disobedience to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Those are the ones who are rightly guided. Where did this come from? He said: A favor and blessing from God. He said: And the hypocrites, God called them all liars in the Qur’an. He said: And immorality means lying in the entire Book of God.

x: God Almighty says: “A bounty and a blessing from God. God is Knowing and Wise.”

God Almighty says: If two groups of the people of faith fight, then make peace between them, O believers, by calling to the rule of God’s Book, and being satisfied with what is in it for and against them. That is making peace between them with justice. But if one of them transgresses against the other means: If these two groups refuse to respond to God’s rule for and against them, and transgresses what God has made just between His creation, and the other responds, then fight the one that transgresses means: Fight the one that transgresses and refuses to respond to God’s rule. until it returns to the command of God means: until it returns to the rule of God that He has made in His Book between His creation. “But if it returns, then make peace between them with justice” means: If the transgressor returns after you have fought them to being satisfied with God’s rule in His Book, then make peace between it and the other group that fought it with justice meaning with fairness between them.
That is the rule of God in His Book that He has made just between His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
And if two parties among the believers should fight
, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the

x: God the Almighty says to the people of faith in Him: The believers are but brothers in religion. “So make peace between your two brothers” if they fight, by compelling them to adhere to the rule of God and the rule of His Messenger. The meaning of two brothers in this context is: every two people of faith who fight. The reciters of the regions read it with the dual vowel.

c: It was reported from Ibn Sirin
m: that he read between your brothers with the letter nun according to the plural form, and this is correct from the Arabic perspective, but it is contrary to what the reciters of the regions do, so I do not like to read it with it. And fear God that you may receive mercy. God the Almighty says: And fear God, O people, by fulfilling His obligations upon you in reconciling between the two people of faith who fight with justice, and in other obligations, and avoiding His transgressions, so that your Lord may have mercy upon you and pardon you for your past crimes if you obey Him, follow His commands and prohibitions, and fear Him by obeying Him.

evidence.text: The reciters of the regions read it with the dual vowel.

It was reported from Ibn Sirin that he read between your brothers with the letter nun according to the plural form, and this is correct from the Arabic perspective, but it is contrary to what the reciters of the regions do, so I do not like to read it with it.

x: He says: The Most High said:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger, let not a believing people ridicule [another] believing people. Perhaps they may be better than them. He says: The one being ridiculed among them is better than the ridiculers. Nor let women ridicule [other] women. He says: Nor let believing women ridicule believing women. Perhaps the one being ridiculed among them may be better than the ridiculers. The commentators differed regarding the mockery that God forbade believers from in this verse.
Some of them said: It is the mockery of the rich by the poor. He forbade mocking the poor for their poverty.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Ibn Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: A people should not mock another people. He said: A people should not mock another people, such that a poor man asks a rich man, or a poor man, and if a man does him a favor for something, then there is nothing wrong with him, so he should not mock him.

x: Others said: Rather, this is a prohibition from God for those who concealed their faults from among the people of faith to mock those among them who uncovered their faults in this world.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
O you who have believed

, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them, he said: Perhaps a man stumbles when he commits a sin; perhaps he is better than them. If his stumble becomes apparent, and you cover up your stumble, perhaps what became apparent will be better for him in the Hereafter with God, and what you cover up will be worse for you. How do you know? Perhaps He will not forgive you. He said: So the man was forbidden from that, and he said: Let not a people ridicule another people; perhaps they may be better than them. And he said the same about women. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God’s prohibition of believers from mocking one another encompasses all meanings of mockery. It is not permissible for a believer to mock another believer, whether for his poverty, or for a sin he has committed, or for any other reason. And His statement,
h
And do not find fault with one another

, means, the Most High says: And do not backbite one another, O believers, and do not slander one another. And He said, Do not find fault with one another, making the one who finds fault with his brother find fault with himself, because the believers are like one man in what they are obligated to do for one another of improving one another's affairs, seeking their betterment, and loving good for one another. For this reason, it was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The believers are like a single body; if one part of it is ill, the rest of the body feels pain and sleeplessness. This is similar to His statement, "
h
O you who have believed
, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except [in lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves," meaning: and do not kill one another.
h
O you who have believed
, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them.
h
And do not insult one another

and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And do not insult one another
, he said: Do not backbite.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not criticize one another
, meaning: Do not insult one another.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement,
h
And do not criticize one another
, means: Do not criticize one another. His statement,
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames

, means: Do not call one another by nicknames. Insulting and nicknames have the same meaning. The plural of nabz is anbaz, and the plural of nickname is alabaqban. The commentators differed regarding the nicknames that God forbade calling one another by in this verse.

x: Some of them said: What is meant by it are the nicknames that are disliked to be used by the one being called. They said: This verse was revealed about a people who had names in the pre-Islamic era, and when they became Muslims, they were forbidden to call one another by the names that were disliked by those names that they were called by in the pre-Islamic era.

Who said that? Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated: Dawud narrated on the authority of ʿAmir: Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak said: “This verse was revealed about us, Banu Salamah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. So if a man called another man by his name, we would say: O Messenger of God, he gets angry at this. So this verse was revealed: ‘
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
’...the entire verse.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Abd al-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak, who said:
m: “The people of the Age of Ignorance used to call men by names. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called a man by one of those names, and they said: O Messenger of God, he gets angry about this. So God revealed: ‘
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
. Evil is the name of disobedience after faith.’”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Amer: Abu Jubayrah Ibn Al-Dahhak told us,
m: and he mentioned something similar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: Abu Jubayrah ibn Ad-Dahhak told me:
m: “The verse, ‘
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames

,’ was revealed concerning Banu Salamah. He said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. He would call a man, and his mother would say, ‘He gets angry with this one.’ So ‘
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
,’ was revealed. And he said on another occasion: If he called one by this name, it would be said, ‘O Messenger of God, he gets angry with this one.’ So the verse was revealed.”

x: Others said: Rather, it is a Muslim man saying to a Muslim man: You are a sinner, you are a fornicator.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us on the authority of Hisin
m: who said: I asked Ikrimah about the statement of God,
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
. He said: It is when a man says to another man, O hypocrite! or O infidel!

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Hisham told us: Hisin told us on the authority of Ikrimah
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
, he said: It is when a man says to another man, O wicked one, O hypocrite.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
. He said: O wicked one, O infidel. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid or Ikrimah,
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
. He said: A man says to another man: O wicked one, O infidel.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
, he said: A man was called an infidel while he was a Muslim.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not insult one another by nicknames
, he says to the man: Do not kill for your Muslim brother: That one is a sinner, that one is a hypocrite. God forbade the Muslim from that and presented it in it.

x: God the Most High says:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger, do not assume too much suspicion of the believers, that is, think ill of them, for the one who assumes it is not right. And God the Most High said: Avoid much suspicion, and He did not say: all suspicion, as He had given permission to the believers to assume good of one another, saying: Why, when you heard it, did not the believing men and believing women think good of one another and say, ‘This is an obvious falsehood?’ (al-Nur 24:12) So God the Most High gave permission to the believers to assume good of one another and to say it, even if they were not certain of what was said about them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the meaning of that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told me: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed
, avoid much [negative] assumption, meaning: God forbade the believer from thinking ill of another believer. His saying,
h
Some suspicion is a sin
, means that if a believer suspects evil of another believer, not good, then it is a sin, because God has forbidden him from doing so, so doing what God has forbidden is a sin. And His statement,
h
And do not spy

, means: Do not seek out the faults of others, nor search for their secrets, seeking thereby to expose their faults. Rather, be content with what is apparent to you of his affair, and praise or blame him based on that, not with what you do not know of his secrets. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not spy
, meaning: God forbade the believer from following the faults of another believer.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And do not spy
, he said: Take what is apparent to you and leave what God has concealed.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, “
h
O you who have believed
, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin.
h
And do not spy
.” Do you know what spying or espionage is? It is to follow or seek out your brother’s fault in order to learn his secret.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And do not spy
. He said: Search. Yunus urged me, saying:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, “
h
O you who have believed
, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin.
h
And do not spy

,” he said: So that I may look into it and ask about it, so that I may know whether it is true or false. He said: So God called it spying. He said: He spies as dogs spy. And he recited the statement of God,
h
And do not spy
or backbite each other. His statement,
h
And do not backbite one another

, means: Do not say things about one another behind the backs of dogs. The one about whom that is said would hate to have it said to his face. In a similar manner to what we said about that, the hadith came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and the people of interpretation said.

x: Mention of who said that, and the trace of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:

c: Yazid bin Mukhallad Al-Rasiti told me: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Tahhan told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin O you
m: who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption, for some assumption is sin.
h
And do not spy

, nor backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. And fear God; indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about backbiting, and he said: It is that you say about your brother what is wrong with him. If you are truthful, then you have backbitten him, and if you are lying, then you have slandered him.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzayʿ told us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-ʿAlaʿ ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us:
m: I heard Al-ʿAla’ narrating, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Do you know what backbiting is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It is mentioning about your brother in a way that is not true. He said: What if what I say about my brother is true? He said: If what you say is true, then you have backbitten him, and if what you say is true, then you have slandered him.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Abbas, on the authority of a man
m: who heard Ibn Umar say: If you mention something about a man, then you have backbitten him, and if you mention something about him that is not in him, then you have slandered him. Shu’bah said another time: If you mention something about him that is not in him, then it is a slander. Abu Musa said: He is Abbas Al-Jariry.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: If you mention the worst things about a man, then you have backbitten him, and if you mention things about him that are not in him, then you have slandered him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: If you say the worst thing about a man, then you have backbitten him, and if you say something that is not true, then you have slandered him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: Backbiting is when someone says the worst thing he knows about him, and slander is when someone says something that is not true.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Mu’awiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Katheer bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Al-Qasim,
m: the freed slave of Mu’awiyah, who said: I heard Ibn Umm Abd say: No one has taken a morsel worse than backbiting a believer.

x: If he says something about him that he knows, then he has backbitten him, and if he says something about him that he does not know, then he has slandered him.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: If you mention something about a man, then you have backbitten him, but if you mention something about him that is not true, then that is slander.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us:
m: I heard Yunus on the authority of al-Hasan that he said about backbiting: It is to mention about your brother what you know of his bad deeds, but if you mention about him what is not in him, then that is slander.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us: Abd Al-Wahid bin Ziyad told us: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us: Hassan bin Al-Mukhariq told us that
m: a woman entered upon Aisha, and when she stood up to leave, Aisha pointed with her hand to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that she was short, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have backbitten her.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: If someone with a amputated hand passed by you and you said: That is the amputated one, then that would be backbiting on your part. He said: I heard Mu’awiyah ibn Qurra say that.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us:
m: I heard Muʿawiyah bin Qurrah say: If a man whose hand had been amputated passed by you and you were to say to him: He has been amputated, you would have slandered him. He said: I mentioned that to Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani and he said: He is telling the truth.

c: Jabir bin Al-Kurdi told me: Ibn Abi Uwais told us: My brother Abu Bakr told me, on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Hamid, on the authority of Musa bin Wardan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: “A man stood in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they saw weakness in his standing, so they said: O Messenger of God, what made so-and-so weak? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have eaten your brother and backbitten him.” Abu Kuraib narrated: Uthman ibn Saeed narrated: Habban ibn Ali al-Anzi narrated: Muthanna ibn Sabah narrated: Amr ibn Shuaib narrated: Muadh ibn al-Jabal said: “We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when the people mentioned a man and said: ‘He only eats what he is fed, and he only rides what he is given to ride, and how weak he is.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘You have backbitten your brother.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, is backbiting him such that we should speak about him?’ He said: ‘It is enough for you to speak about your brother as he is.’”

evidence.text: He said: I heard Mu’awiyah ibn Qurra say that.

x: God Almighty says: O mankind, indeed We created you from a male fluid from men and a female fluid from women. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hisham told us: Ubayd God ibn Musa told us: Uthman ibn al-Aswad told us on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: God created the child from the man’s semen and the woman’s semen, and He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us: Uthman bin Al-Aswad told us on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, he said: God did not create the child except from the sperm of the man and the woman together, because God says, We created you from a male and a female. And His statement,
h
And We have made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another

, means: And We have made you related, so some of you are related to others by distant lineage, and some of you are related to others by close lineage. So the one who is related by distant lineage is the one who is not related by the peoples of the peoples, and that is if it is said to a man from the Arabs: From which people are you? He says: I am from Mudar, or from Rabi’ah. As for the people of close lineage, they are the people of the tribes, and they are like Tamim from Mudar, and Bakr from Rabi’ah, and the closest tribes are the clans, and they are like Shaiban from Bakr and Darim from Tamim, and something similar to that is the saying of Ibn Ahmar al-Bahili: From the people of Hamdan, or Saad Al-Ashirah, or Khawlan, or Madhhij, they were excited for him In a similar vein to what we said about the meaning of His statement,
h
And We made you into peoples and tribes
, he said: The people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us: Abu Hasin told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And We made you peoples and tribes
. He said: Peoples are groups, and tribes are clans.
b.via: Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Khallad bin Aslam told us: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And We made you peoples and tribes
, he said: Peoples means the group. Khallad said: Abu Bakr said: The great tribes, like Banu Tamim, and the tribes mean the clans.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Atiyah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And We made you peoples and tribes
. He said: The peoples are the masses, and the tribes are the individuals.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Peoples, he said: distant lineage. And tribes less than that.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We made you peoples and tribes
. He said: Peoples are distant relatives, and tribes are like his saying: So-and-so is from the Banu

x: God Almighty says:
h
The Bedouins said

: We believe in God and His Messenger, so we are believers. God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to them: You have not believed and you are not believers, but say: We have submitted. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about the Banu Asad Bedouins.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The Bedouins said

, ‘We believe,’ he said: The Bedouins of Banu Asad bin Khuzaymah. The commentators differed about the reason why it was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Tell these Bedouins: Say, ‘We have submitted,’ and do not say, ‘We believe.’”

x: Some of them said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only ordered this because the people had believed with their tongues, but their words had not been confirmed by their actions. So it was said to them: Say, ‘We have submitted,’ because Islam is a statement, and faith is a statement and an action.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: h
The Bedouins said
, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: Islam is the word, and faith is the action.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of al-Zuhri

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, and al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Amir ibn Sa'd, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to some men, but did not give anything to any other man. Sa'd said: 'O Messenger of God, you gave to so-and-so and so-and-so, but did not give anything to so-and-so, and he is a believer.' The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Or a Muslim.' Until Sa'd repeated it three times, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Or a Muslim.' Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'I give to some men and leave out those who are dearer to me than them. I do not give them anything for fear that they will fall on their faces into the Fire.'"

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
The desert Arabs say
, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed.’ He said: They did not confirm their belief with their deeds. So God responded to them with, Say, ‘You have not believed; but say, ‘We have submitted.’

c: And He informed them that
m: the believers are those who believed in God and His Messenger and then did not doubt, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, those are the truthful ones. They confirmed their belief with their deeds. So whoever among them says, ‘I am a believer,’ has spoken the truth. He said: As for whoever claims to believe through words but does not act, then he has lied and is not truthful.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: But say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: It is Islam.

x: Others said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that this be said to them because they wanted to be called by the names of the emigrants before they emigrated, so God informed them that they would have the names of the Bedouins, not the names of the emigrants.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Bedouins said

, ‘We believe.’... the verse. This is because they wanted to be called by the name of the migration, and not by the names that God had given them, and that was at the beginning of the migration, but rather for the inheritance to be given to them.

x: Others said: They were told that because they had shown favor to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by their conversion to Islam. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell them that you did not believe, but rather submitted out of fear of being taken captive and killed.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
The Bedouins say

, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed.’ By my life, this verse does not include all Bedouins. There are some Bedouins who believe in God and the Last Day. Rather, it was revealed about a tribe of Bedouins who boasted about their Islam to the
h
The desert Arabs say
, "We believe." Say, "You do not believe; but say, 'We submit,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts.
h
And if you obey God and His Messenger
h
He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds

. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful." Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said, We have submitted, but we did not fight you, as the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so fought you. So God said, Do not say, ‘We believe,’ but say, ‘We have submitted,’ until it reaches your hearts.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: This verse does not apply to the Bedouins. There are some Bedouins who believe in God and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of drawing closer to God. However, it applies to groups of Bedouins.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Rabah, on the authority of Abu Auf, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
The Bedouins say
, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: We submitted out of fear of being taken captive and killed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Say ‘We have submitted.’ He said: We have surrendered. Yunus narrated: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: He recited the statement of God, Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, “We have submitted,’ meaning we have entered into peace and abandoned fighting and fighting by saying, ‘There is no god but God.’” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ Then if they say, ‘There is no god but God,’ their blood and property are protected from me, except for what is due, and their reckoning is with God.” The most correct of the sayings in interpreting the statement we mentioned from Al-Zuhri is that God proceeded to these Bedouins who entered the religion by their acknowledgement of the word, and did not confirm their word with their actions, to say in general terms, We believe, without restricting their saying to that, by saying, We believe in God and His Messenger. But He commanded them to say the statement that would not be difficult for its listeners and in which the one who said it was right, which is to say, We have submitted, meaning: We have entered the religion and the wealth, and the true testimony. And His statement,
h
And when faith has not yet entered your hearts
, God Almighty says: And when knowledge of the laws of faith and the truths of its meanings has not yet entered your hearts. And His statement,
h
And if you obey God and His Messenger
h
He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds

, means that God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these Bedouins who say, We believe, but faith has not yet entered their hearts: If you obey God and His Messenger, O people, and follow His command and the command of His Messenger, and learn what He has enjoined upon you, and refrain from what He has forbidden you,
h
He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds

, meaning, He will not wrong you in any way from the reward for your deeds, nor will He diminish you in any way from their reward. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
He will not deprive you
: He will not diminish you.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds
, meaning: He will not wrong you in any of your deeds.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about
h
And if you obey God and His Messenger

, he said: If you confirm your faith with your deeds, that will be accepted from you. The reading of the regions is La ya’alatum min 3amalakum without a hamza or an alif, except for Abu Amr, who read it La ya’alatum with an alif, taking into consideration his statement And We did not deprive them of anything of their work At-Tur 52:21. So whoever says alat, says ya’alat. As for the others, they made that from Lat yalit, as Ru’bah ibn al-’Ajaj said: And a dewy night I walked, and it did not turn me away from its secret. I wish The correct statement in our view on this matter is what is read in Medina and Kufa as la yaltum without an alif or a hamza, in the language of those who say la yalita do not let me sleep, for two reasons: First: The consensus of the most eloquent reciters on this. Second: It is in the Mushaf without an alif, and the hamza is not dropped in such a place because it is quiescent, and when the hamza is quiescent it remains, as you say ta’murun you command and ta’akulun you eat. It is only dropped if what precedes it is quiescent. A letter in the Qur’an that comes in one language does not carry over another that comes in a different language if both languages are known in the speech of the Arabs. We have already mentioned that al-ta and la-ta are two well-known languages of their speech. And His statement, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, means the Most High says: Indeed, God is Forgiving, O Arabs, to whoever obeys Him and repents to Him for his past sins, so obey Him and abide by His commands and prohibitions, and He will forgive you your sins. He is Merciful to His creation who repent to Him, and He does not punish them after their repentance from their sins, for what they repented from, so repent to Him and He will have mercy on you.

evidence.text: The reading of the regions is La ya’alatum min 3amalakum without a hamza or an alif, except for Abu Amr, who read it La ya’alatum with an alif, taking into consideration his statement And We did not deprive them of anything of their work At-Tur 52:21.

I wish The correct statement in our view on this matter is what is read in Medina and Kufa as la yaltum without an alif or a hamza, in the language of those who say la yalita do not let me sleep, for two reasons: First: The consensus of the most eloquent reciters on this.

x: God Almighty says to the Bedouins who said, We believe, but faith has not yet entered their hearts: The believers, O people, are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger, and then have not doubted, meaning: then have not doubted the Oneness of God, nor the Prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and have committed themselves to obeying God and obeying His Messenger, and to doing what is required of them of God's obligations without doubting that this is required of them. And strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, meaning: they strive against the polytheists by spending their wealth and sacrificing their lives in striving against them, in the way God has commanded them to strive against them, and that is His way so that the word of God will be supreme, and the word of those who disbelieve will be lowest. And his saying,
h
Those are the truthful ones

, means: Those who do that are the truthful ones in their saying, We are believers, not those who entered the nation out of fear of the sword in order to protect their blood and property. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
Those are the truthful ones
, that they confirmed their faith with their deeds.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to these Bedouins who say, We believe, but faith has not yet entered their hearts: Do you know God? O people, about your religion, meaning about your obedience to your Lord? And God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. He says: And God, whom you know that you are believers, is All-Knowing of everything in the seven heavens and the seven earths. Nothing of it is hidden from Him. So how can you know Him about your religion and the faith that you are upon, while nothing is hidden from Him, in the heavens or the earth, so what you are upon of religion is hidden from Him? And God is Knowing of all things. He says: And God is All-Knowing of everything that was and is and of what will be. This is a command from God to these Bedouins to forbid them from lying and saying other than what they are upon in their religion. He says: God is all-knowing and encompasses everything, so beware of saying anything contrary to what He knows in your hearts, lest you be punished, for nothing is hidden from Him.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: These Bedouins, O Muhammad, have bestowed upon you a favor by converting to Islam. “Say, ‘Do not bestow upon me your Islam. Rather, God bestows upon you that He has guided you to faith.’” He says: Rather, God bestows upon you, O people, that He has guided you to faith in Him and in His Messenger, if you should be truthful. He says: If you are truthful in what you say, ‘We have believed,’ then it is God who bestowed upon you a favor by guiding you to Him. So do not bestow upon me a favor by your Islam. He mentioned that these Bedouins from Banu Asad had shown the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a favor, and said: We believed without fighting, and we did not fight you as others did. So God revealed these verses about them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding this verse,
h
They do you a favor by becoming Muslims
. Are they Banu Asad? He said: That has been said.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sahl bin Yusuf told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Bishr:
m: I said to Sa’id bin Jubayr, “They do you a favor by converting to Islam. Are they the Banu Asad?” He said, They claim that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Umrah, who said:
m: Bishr ibn Ghalib and Labid ibn Uttar, or Bishr ibn Uttar and Labid ibn Ghalib, were sitting with Al-Hajjaj. Bishr ibn Ghalib said to Labid ibn Uttar: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers… was revealed about your people, Banu Tamim. I mentioned that to Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and he said: If he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered him:
h
They do you a favor by becoming Muslims
. They said: We have become Muslims and we have not fought you, Banu Asad.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: And do not wish that we had converted to Islam without fighting. We did not fight you as the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so fought you. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: “Do not wish me to have your Islam. Rather, God has bestowed upon you a favour by guiding you to faith.”
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, “
h
They do you a favor by becoming Muslims
. Say, ‘Do not do me a favor by becoming Muslims.’” He said: These verses were revealed about the Bedouins.

x: God the Almighty says: O Arabs, God knows not who among you is truthful and who is lying, and who among you has entered the religion of Islam out of desire for it, and who has entered it out of fear of our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his soldiers. So do not teach us your religion and the secrets in your hearts, for God knows what is concealed in your hearts and what you tell yourselves, and He knows what is hidden from you. So, conceal your secrets in the heavens and the earth, and nothing of that is hidden from Him. And God is Seeing of what you do. He says: God is All-Seeing of your deeds that you do, whether you do them openly or secretly, whether you do obedience or disobedience, and He is with you in all of that, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, and He is its equal. I deny his statement, They do you a favor because they have submitted in the accusative case because they do them a favor upon it.

He mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, it is they do you a favor because they have submitted, and that is evidence for the correctness of what we have said. If it were said: It is accusative meaning: They do you a favor because they have submitted, then that would be a correct interpretation.

Some of the Arabists said: It is in the genitive case, meaning because they have submitted. As for the an in His statement, Rather, God has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you, it is in the accusative case due to the omission of the relative clause, because the meaning of the statement is: Rather, God has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith.

evidence.text: He mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, it is they do you a favor because they have submitted, and that is evidence for the correctness of what we have said.

notes.en: That is, you are close to one another: all of you, in your descent from one father, share the same limitations and fall short of perfection. He likened your deficiency to a measure that has not been filled. Then He made clear that distinction is based not on lineage but on piety. Al-Nihāyah (3/129).
